legal_findings: December18 1998 report submission is affirmatively supported by the signed co-chair letter addressed to the Vice President; release that day is separately recorded. Receipt is not proved and is not an express additional statutory trigger. Under parent section4, thirty days after submission gives January17 1999 if no earlier valid ending or later Presidential extension controls.

A subordinate charter cannot itself rewrite Presidential commands. The later Presidential December31 reporting deadline strongly supports continuing Presidential authority beyond the older October31 charter date. Nonetheless, a deadline and administrative authorization duration are distinct provisions; the later amendment does not expressly restate the charter or sunset. Parent section3(e) delegates FACA functions, making exact charter authority and final operative terms relevant.

The retained charter says October31 unless properly renewed while the same report describes later Presidential instructions and November9 work. Inconsistent charter footnote chronology and an archive page mixing January1999 update/December release with old October dates warn that these are consolidated or stale representations. Work occurrence alone does not establish lawful charter renewal.

The frozen record does not conclusively resolve whether the charter date was superseded, renewed, or independently limited charter-based operation. Neither October31 nor January17 is promoted to an established first cessation. EO13138 sections3(b),9 supports formal revocation September30 and prior completion, without dating earliest cessation.
residuals: Reports/recommendations, independent Benton institutional-memory activity and any accrued support/expense consequences do not create continuing Committee authority. No specific unpaid liability is established.
scientific_gaps: Resolve final charter/renewal terms or competent applicable FACA authority sufficiently to reconcile the October31 language with later Presidential instructions. Equivalent legal evidence can resolve the issue; a particular document is not demanded mechanically.
